Closest to style frame B; builds Goldie streams, gut cells, body layers, 95%, BBB.
Closest to style frame C; builds letter, stamp, headline, newspapers; the sensitive scene, reviewed early.

Lab, capsules, chart on the ripple baseline, GRAS with the existing stamp.

lines.text: For fifty years, three little letters have terrified dinner tables.

lines.text: MSG. The most misunderstood molecule in your kitchen.

shots.on_screen: A single gold drop falls into a broth surface on 'MSG.'; the Fifth Ripple spreads (4 white rings, the fifth gold and wider); Goldie pops up out of the centre.

lines.text: MSG. The most misunderstood molecule in your kitchen.

shots.hero: Title: Goldie and the Fifth Ripple

lines.text: In 1908, a Japanese chemist named Kikunae Ikeda noticed something odd about his seaweed soup.

shots.on_screen: 1908: a bright period laboratory-kitchen; Kikunae Ikeda (respectful paper doll: high collar, round glasses, moustache) carries a steaming bowl of seaweed soup to his desk.

lines.text: In 1908, a Japanese chemist named Kikunae Ikeda noticed something odd about his seaweed soup.

shots.on_screen: Ikeda sips; a kombu-green strip floats in the bowl; his eyebrows lift and a '?' cut-out pops on 'odd'.

lines.text: It wasn't sweet, sour, salty or bitter. It was something else.

shots.on_screen: Fifth Ripple motif: rings spread from the bowl, each carrying a taste icon that pops on its word (candy = sweet, lemon = sour, salt crystal = salty, coffee bean = bitter). On 'something else' the fifth ring blooms wide and gold and a tiny Goldie rises from the centre.

layout.MID: Bowl + rings -> fifth gold ring + Goldie

shots.camera: Locked overhead, slight push-in on the fifth ring.
shots.notes: Icons only, no words: captions say them.

lines.text: So he boiled down a mountain of seaweed, and found the culprit: glutamic acid.

shots.on_screen: A mountain of kombu-green seaweed strips tumbles from the top of frame into a giant pot; Ikeda is tiny beside it.
shots.camera: Tilt down with the falling seaweed.

lines.text: So he boiled down a mountain of seaweed, and found the culprit: glutamic acid.

shots.on_screen: Time-lapse: the pile boils down in paper steam puffs to a dish of crystals; Goldie peeks out and a flat cut-paper skeletal diagram of glutamic acid slides in beside it.

lines.text: He named the taste umami, and paired it with sodium to make a seasoning.

shots.on_screen: Ikeda holds up the crystal dish; the fifth gold ring returns behind it. Then Goldie meets a small blue sodium ion and they link mittens on 'sodium'.

lines.text: Monosodium glutamate.

shots.on_screen: Goldie and the sodium ion hop into the MSG shaker (first canonical appearance); its cap snaps on.

lines.text: Which sounds alarmingly chemical.

shots.on_screen: 'Alarmingly chemical': the shaker sprouts bubbling lab flasks; Goldie looks nervous; a tomato-red warning card flaps.
shots.transition_in: Paper slide (sheet slides over, shadow leading)

lines.text: But glutamate is one of the most common amino acids on Earth.

shots.on_screen: Flasks fall away; zoom out: Goldie is one bead in a long chain of vivid amino-acid beads that wraps around a paper Earth.

lines.text: It's in tomatoes, mushrooms, parmesan, even human breast milk.

shots.on_screen: A 2x2 grid fills cell by cell, each food with a mini Goldie peeking out: tomato, mushrooms, parmesan, a simple milk-drop / baby-bottle icon.
shots.notes: Icon-level milk; no nudity. No amounts, no ranking.

lines.text: And to your body, glutamate from a tomato and from MSG is exactly the same molecule.

shots.on_screen: Top half: a tomato releases a Goldie. Bottom half: the MSG shaker shakes out a Goldie. Each stands beside the same skeletal diagram.

lines.text: And to your body, glutamate from a tomato and from MSG is exactly the same molecule.

shots.on_screen: Divider tears away; the two Goldies and their diagrams slide together and overlap perfectly; an '=' cut-out.

scenes.title: What Happens When You Eat It

lines.text: So what happens when you eat it?

shots.on_screen: A fork lifts a bite sprinkled with tiny Goldies up to a paper-doll mouth in profile.

lines.text: Your tongue tastes it, and tells your brain: protein!

shots.on_screen: Tongue landscape: Goldies land on receptor cups, each dock sends a small gold Fifth Ripple; a signal zips up a brush-stroke nerve to a pink paper brain that pops a speech slip.

lines.text: Then it reaches your gut... and gets eaten.

shots.on_screen: The camera dives down through layered pink paper into the gut; on 'eaten' the first gut cell chomps a Goldie.

lines.text: The cells lining your intestines burn glutamate as fuel. Around ninety-five percent never even makes it into your blood.

shots.on_screen: Style frame B: turquoise sky over pink villi; gut cells with white bibs on two tiers; a stream of Goldies drifts in; the front cell chomps one with happy arc eyes, the next one wears a gold flame (burning fuel).

layout.MID: Back tier of 3 cells + Goldie stream

shots.hero: Gut cells eat glutamate as fuel (style frame B)

lines.text: The cells lining your intestines burn glutamate as fuel. Around ninety-five percent never even makes it into your blood.

shots.on_screen: Pull back: the gut wall as a pink border; a big Young Serif number rolls up and lands on '95%'; below the wall a coral blood vessel gets only a trickle of one or two Goldies on 'blood'.

lines.text: And the rest hits the blood-brain barrier, one of the best-guarded borders in your body.

shots.on_screen: Track up the vessel with the few remaining Goldies to the head; a cobalt cut-paper castle wall rises across the frame.

lines.text: And the rest hits the blood-brain barrier, one of the best-guarded borders in your body.

shots.on_screen: Paper-doll guards (mitten hands, friendly) at the gate; a Goldie approaches, a guard raises a mitten, Goldie bounces back and shrugs.

lines.text: Scientists have tested it again and again, in double-blind studies where nobody knows who got the real thing.

shots.on_screen: Bright lab on a cobalt graph-paper grid; scientists in all three skin tones run tests; clipboards flip with ticks on each 'again'.
shots.transition_in: Paper slide (sheet slides over, shadow leading)

lines.text: Scientists have tested it again and again, in double-blind studies where nobody knows who got the real thing.

shots.on_screen: Two identical capsules drop under two cups and shuffle; scientist and volunteer both wear paper blindfolds (nobody knows).

lines.text: People who said they were sensitive to MSG reacted just as often to the fake.

shots.on_screen: Two tiers of volunteers (all three skin tones) with worried thought bubbles take their cups.

shots.on_screen: A flattened Fifth Ripple becomes the chart baseline; a gold bar (Goldie sticker = MSG) and a cobalt bar (placebo) rise to nearly the same height.

lines.text: Today, the FDA classifies MSG as generally recognized as safe. Just like salt and sugar.

shots.on_screen: A generic official document slides in (no seal, no logo); the distressed rubber stamp slams on.

lines.text: So how did a seaweed seasoning become a villain?

shots.on_screen: A kombu strip curls into the MSG shaker; a tomato-red spotlight snaps on and a cut-paper villain moustache drops onto it.
shots.transition_in: Paper slide (sheet slides over, shadow leading)

lines.text: In 1968, a doctor wrote to a medical journal. After eating at Chinese restaurants, he felt numb and weak.

shots.on_screen: Cobalt desk: a lemon letter on a hot-pink underlay slides in and writes itself in squiggle lines (no legible text); it folds into an envelope addressed in squiggles on 'journal'.
shots.notes: Author not named or drawn; journal not named.

lines.text: In 1968, a doctor wrote to a medical journal. After eating at Chinese restaurants, he felt numb and weak.

shots.on_screen: Two small cut-paper symptom icons pin onto the letter: a mitten hand with pins-and-needles dots (numb) on 'numb', a drooping arm (weak) on 'weak'.
shots.notes: SENSITIVE: no restaurant, no people, no 'oriental' signifiers - paper and objects only.

lines.text: Was it the wine? The salt? The MSG? It was a guess.

shots.on_screen: The turquoise card from style frame C: wine bottle, salt cellar, MSG shaker; an ink '?' drops over each on its word, then the three merge into one wobbly '?'.

lines.text: But the journal gave it a catchy headline: Chinese Restaurant Syndrome.

shots.on_screen: Style frame C: the stamp handle slams the quoted headline across the letter; paper flecks fly; coral newspapers start sliding out from the stamp like a tomato-red anti-ripple.
shots.notes: Young Serif, hyphenated, in quotes; framed as the thing being criticised.

lines.text: Then scientists injected huge doses into newborn mice, and found brain damage.

shots.on_screen: A bright lab: pink newborn mouse pups in a nest; a comically giant syringe lowers from the top (never touches them). On 'brain damage' the coral newspapers sliding around the edges grow bigger tomato-red headline bars.

lines.text: Scary. Until you remember that a baby mouse injection is nothing like dinner.

shots.on_screen: Top: giant syringe over a tiny mouse pup. Bottom: a dinner bowl with a spoon and Goldies, and a tiny gut cell with a bib chomping one (callback to s05). A big '≠' cut-out on the divider.

lines.text: And nobody panicked about tomato sauce or parmesan. The fear stuck to one cuisine, and the name said it out loud.

shots.on_screen: Top: pasta with tomato sauce and parmesan under a silent tomato-red bell. Bottom: a plain white takeout carton under the same bell, ringing. Identical Goldies float over both.

lines.text: And nobody panicked about tomato sauce or parmesan. The fear stuck to one cuisine, and the name said it out loud.

scenes.title: So... Is MSG Bad for You?

lines.text: So, is MSG bad for you?
Not really.

shots.transition_in: Paper slide (sheet slides over, shadow leading)

lines.text: It's a story about how one guess, a catchy name, and a little prejudice outlived decades of science.

continuity.name: Goldie, the broth droplet

continuity.rules: Flat cut-paper five-carbon zigzag beside Goldie when chemistry matters (s03, s04), so the droplet is never read as the literal molecule.

allowed_numbers_and_claims: s01: the three puppets' claims (fictional, DRAMATIZATION); 'for fifty years' -> label '50 years'
s03: 1908; Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda; seaweed soup; not sweet/sour/salty/bitter but 'something else'; boiled down seaweed; glutamic acid; named umami; paired with sodium -> monosodium glutamate
s04: glutamate is one of the most common amino acids on Earth; in tomatoes, mushrooms, parmesan, human breast milk; tomato glutamate = MSG glutamate
s05: tongue tastes it -> brain: protein; gut cells burn it as fuel; ~95% never reaches the blood; the rest hits the blood-brain barrier, one of the best-guarded borders
s07: double-blind studies; MSG-sensitive people reacted as often to placebo; FDA: generally recognized as safe (GRAS), like salt and sugar
s08: ~1/3 the sodium of table salt; swap some in: same flavour, less sodium

s06: 1968 letter from a doctor to a medical journal; felt numb and weak after eating at Chinese restaurants; wine/salt/MSG was a guess; the journal's headline 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome'; scientists injected huge doses into newborn mice and found brain damage; a mouse injection is nothing like dinner; nobody panicked about tomato sauce or parmesan
s09: 'Not really'; one guess, a catchy name and a little prejudice outlived decades of science; next time you see a No MSG sign, maybe reach for the shaker
forbidden: Anything the rewrite cut: Tokyo label, 'within a year', soy sauce, '~10x' milk, 'body makes its own', palpitations, the journal's name, 1969, 'Italian Restaurant Syndrome', baking powder, 'even water', 'tomato on your pizza', huge doses on an empty stomach, 'savory' (cut from s03), 'more than fifty years'.
Any number, %, axis value, study count, dose or date not listed above; never '5%'.
Health claims beyond the script; real logos, seals, mastheads, networks, platforms or brands; recognisable real people.
Gore: no needle touching an animal.
Dull colours (grey, beige, cream, muddy brown, desaturated); glows and gradients (Kombu Paper is flat paper).
More than one 1-3 word label at a time (the DRAMATIZATION line in the lower third is the only extra text).
guardrails.dramatization: Every frame with a readable puppet (s01.01-04 and s01.07, s09.01, s09.03) carries the torn-paper lower third with the role and 'DRAMATIZATION - fictional character'.
sensitive_1960s_section: s06 shows only paper, type, a bottle, a salt cellar, a shaker, mice, food and a plain white carton: no restaurants, no staff, no diners.
No faux-Asian fonts or signifiers (pagodas, lanterns, dragons, chopsticks as decoration, conical hats); the carton is plain white.
The headline is quoted, hyphenated and stamped as the thing being criticised; never a joke or a brand.
The prejudice beat is a bell over one food and silence over another; no people are shown being othered.
Ikeda is drawn respectfully; the letter author and the mouse researchers are never named or drawn.
